name: healthy-ai-code-mcp
description: MCP server that analyses code health in real time, guiding AI assistants and developers to write clean, maintainable code. Provides objective 1-10 health scores, deep smell detection, pre-commit gates, branch-level change analysis, bus-factor mapping, and ROI-backed refactoring business cases.

tools.name: code_health_score
tools.description: Fast 1-10 code health screening for a single file or snippet. Returns an objective health score without full diagnostic output — use for quick checks before deciding whether a deep review is needed.

tools.name: code_health_review
tools.description: Deep code health inspection that detects smells, complexity hotspots, coupling issues, and duplication. Returns actionable refactoring suggestions and a loopComplete flag. Call in a loop until loopComplete is true to surface all issues.

tools.name: pre_commit_code_health_safeguard
tools.description: Pre-commit quality gate that evaluates all staged files. Returns pass, warn, or block per file. Blocks commit when any file scores below 7.0, ensuring regressions never reach version control.

tools.name: analyze_change_set
tools.description: Branch-level health analysis comparing changed files against a base branch. Returns per-file health deltas, regressions, and improvements — designed to run before opening or merging a pull request.

tools.name: code_health_refactoring_business_case
tools.description: Generates a business-case document for a proposed refactoring, including estimated time saved, defect risk reduction, and ROI. Use when refactoring work needs to be justified to stakeholders or engineering management.

tools.name: explain_code_health
tools.description: Plain-language explanation of the 1-10 code health scale: what each score band means, how scores are calculated, and why the thresholds (7.0 commit minimum, 9.5 AI-ready target) were chosen.

tools.name: explain_code_health_productivity
tools.description: Explains the research-backed relationship between code health and developer productivity, including effects on cycle time, defect rates, and onboarding speed. Use when a team questions whether health scores justify investment.

tools.name: code_health_knowledge_map
tools.description: Analyses code ownership and contribution patterns to identify knowledge silos and bus-factor risk across the codebase. Use when planning staffing changes, onboarding new engineers, or assessing handover readiness.

tools.name: code_health_method_coupling
tools.description: Detect methods that always change together (temporal coupling) using git history

tools.name: code_health_architecture_debt
tools.description: Analyses module-level architecture debt: FAN-IN/OUT ratios, Propagation Cost (transitive impact), cyclic dependencies via Tarjan SCC, and Cost-of-Change score per file. Use when planning large refactors or evaluating architectural health of a codebase.

directory.description: Absolute path to the project root directory

maxFiles.description: Maximum number of files to analyse (default: 1000)

tools.name: code_health_bus_factor
tools.description: Analyses bus factor, sprint-level developer congestion, and knowledge loss index for a project. Uses Shannon entropy to measure knowledge concentration and identifies files at risk if key contributors leave.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project git root directory

filePattern.description: Glob pattern for files to analyse (default: **/*.{ts,js,py})

maxFiles.description: Maximum number of files to analyse (default: 100)

includeKnowledgeLossIndex.description: Include inactive-contributor ratio via git blame (default: true)

tools.name: code_health_ai_readiness
tools.description: Calculates an AI-Readiness Score (0–10) for a directory. Composite metric measuring how well a codebase suits AI-assisted development: naming clarity, type coverage, context window fit, doc signal, and modularity. Returns score, per-dimension breakdown, AI-blockers, and a summary.

directory.description: Absolute path to the directory to analyse

language.description: Primary language to filter files on (default: typescript)

maxFiles.description: Maximum number of files to analyse (default: 200)

tools.name: code_health_hotspots
tools.description: Identifies the hottest code areas in a git repo: files with high complexity AND high change frequency. Combines cyclomatic complexity with churn rate over a configurable time period. Top-N hotspots returned sorted by score (0–1).

repoPath.description: Absolute path to the git repository root

packageRoot.description: Limit analysis to a sub-path for monorepo support (e.g. 'packages/core')

minChurnCommits.description: Minimum commits to include a file (default: 3)

tools.name: code_health_trend_analysis
tools.description: Analyses how a file's code quality changes over time. Returns complexity trend (slope, rising/stable/declining) and an overall health trajectory per file. Supports analysis of up to 20 files per call.

repoPath.description: Absolute path to the git repository root

filePaths.description: List of file paths to analyse (relative to repoPath)

samplePoints.description: Number of sampling points for complexity trend (default: 5)
